title: Highest temperature in London on August 26?
description:

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office forecasts for London on August 26 indicate a daytime maximum near 26°C under unsettled conditions with bands of heavy showers and thunderstorms expected to track northward. These thundery plumes, driven by warm, humid air and residual Atlantic frontal influences, introduce localized variability in cloud cover and timing that can shift peak readings by 1–2°C. Ensemble models show close clustering around this value, consistent with late-summer patterns where above-average warmth persists yet rainfall interrupts full solar heating. Traders have assigned the highest implied probability to 26°C because official guidance centers there while acknowledging modest downside risk from prolonged cloud or showers and limited upside from clearer intervals. Updated model runs and Met Office briefings remain the key near-term catalysts.

**Trader consensus centers on 38–39°C as the most probable peak temperature for Chongqing on August 26, 2026, reflecting official forecasts under persistent subtropical high pressure tempered by scattered rain from the peripheral influence of tropical storm Zitan (紫檀).**

Chongqing Meteorological Observatory projections show most areas reaching 22–40°C locally on the 26th, with the urban core forecast at 28–39°C amid mostly cloudy to clear conditions and isolated thunderstorms. Recent days have already delivered highs of 37–39.9°C, establishing a strong baseline. Model consensus points to intensification potential limited by increased cloud cover and moisture, reducing the likelihood of widespread 40°C readings while supporting 38°C as the modal outcome. Historical August climatology for the region (typical peaks near 31–35°C) underscores the current anomaly driven by the dominant high-pressure ridge. Upcoming official station reports and any revised model runs on the 26th could shift probabilities if convective activity suppresses maxima more than expected or if clearer skies allow greater heating. Market-implied odds closely track these dynamical and thermodynamic factors, weighting the balance between radiative heating and localized cooling from showers.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Zhengzhou Xinzheng International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 26 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zhcc

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models and observational data from sources including WeatherBug, PredictWind, and regional meteorological services indicate a high of 32–34 °C for Zhengzhou on August 26, driven by persistent summer warmth under partly cloudy skies with limited precipitation expected. This aligns with typical late-August climatology for the region, where average daily highs reach about 32 °C amid high humidity and weak synoptic forcing. The dominant market-implied probability for 32 °C or higher (94 %) reflects trader consensus on these stable atmospheric conditions and the narrow uncertainty range in short-term numerical weather prediction. A realistic challenge would require an unforecasted surge in cloud cover or convective rainfall timing that suppresses peak heating, though current model agreement makes a drop below 32 °C unlikely.
